chunks: What the Sheikh (may Allah the Exalted support him) informed me of, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who inserts his hand into a vessel while it is impure. He said: 'The vessel should be overturned [and its contents discarded].'

key_terms.اَلشَّيْخُ: the Sheikh (here: likely Sheikh al-Mufid, al-Tusi's teacher)
key_terms.يُكْفِئُ: to overturn, to tip and empty (discarding the impure contents)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia fiqh when an impure hand is inserted into a vessel of water?
ai.summary: Al-Bazanti reports asking Imam al-Ridha (AS) about the ruling when a man inserts his impure (najis) hand into a vessel of water. The Imam ruled that the vessel must be overturned and its contents discarded, establishing that contact of a najis hand renders the vessel's water ritually impure and unfit for use.
